qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Deeply entrenched B2B credit scoring standard with high switching costs across banking and mortgage underwriting. Empirically demonstrated by 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 54.0% (FY25 ROIC 80.9%) and EBIT margins expanding to 46%+. However, moat faces active erosion as FHFA and GSEs approved competitor VantageScore 4.0, directly dismantling FICO's statutory monopoly in residential mortgage originations.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Classic cautionary tale of an over-milked toll booth. After exploiting its monopoly by hiking mortgage scoring prices by >400%, FICO triggered regulatory backlash: the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) mandated the adoption of rival VantageScore 4.0 for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac loan deliveries, ending FICO's decades-long sole-source monopoly. In 2025–2026, FHFA expanded VantageScore 4.0 to all GSE lenders with aligned pricing grids, while major lenders (e.g. Rocket Mortgage) began active deployment. Concurrently, aggressive pricing provoked DOJ/FTC antitrust scrutiny and congressional probes. These terminal competitive and regulatory headwinds reduce persistence well below 15 years, capping CAP at 10. Downstream gates bypassed per strict waterfall.
qualitative.evidence: FY2025 revenue reached $1.99B with EBIT of $924.9M and Net Income of $651.9M. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 54.0% (FY2025: 80.9%), and FCF conversion is 89.9% ($613.2M FCF). Despite historic capital efficiency, FICO faces severe structural terminal headwinds. The FHFA credit score modernization framework broke FICO's sole-source GSE mortgage standard by authorizing VantageScore 4.0 (jointly developed by credit bureaus Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion), with GSEs rolling out unified pricing grids and all-lender availability through 2025-2026. Lenders like Rocket Mortgage are actively moving volume to VantageScore. Furthermore, rapid price hikes to $10/score sparked congressional antitrust investigations and requests for FTC/DOJ action, forcing FICO to defensively freeze pricing for its Preferred Program. Capital allocation also exhibits severe financial engineering: aggressive share repurchases executed at peak valuations (>50-80x P/E) pushed long-term debt to $2.66B against only $134M cash ($2.52B net debt, ~3.9x Net Income), resulting in -$1.75B in negative stockholders' equity.
